facts.text: The Houston Energy Corridor sprang to life in the late 1960s and 1970s, when Interstate 10 expansion opened up former rural land for oil and gas commerce.
When Hurricane Harvey hit in 2017, historic rainfall overwhelmed the Addicks and Barker reservoirs, flooding the Energy Corridor and testing its flood‑control system.
The corridor houses more than 26 million square feet of office space, supporting over 105,000 jobs across the region.
Over 26,000 acres of urban parkland border the corridor, including George Bush Park and Bear Creek Pioneers Park along Buffalo Bayou.
BP America, Citgo, ConocoPhillips, Nouryon and Shell USA all maintain major operations within the Energy Corridor.
METRO provides bus service to the Energy Corridor, connecting commuters to downtown Houston and surrounding suburbs.
